question_text: A plane mirror is placed on the $x\text{-}z$ plane and is free to rotate about the $z$-axis. A fixed object is on the $x\text{-}y$ plane at a point $O(5\text{ m}, 5\text{ m})$. When the mirror starts rotating anticlockwise with an angular speed of $5\text{ rad/s}$ about the $z$-axis, the initial linear speed of the image is
diagram_description: A 3D coordinate frame showing the x, y, and z axes, with the mirror lying initially in the x-z plane and a fixed point object O located at coordinates (5 m, 5 m) in the x-y plane.
solution: Distance of the image from the rotation axis is $r = \sqrt{5^2 + 5^2} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ m}$. When the mirror rotates at $\omega$, the image rotates at $2\omega = 10\text{ rad/s}$, giving $v = (2\omega)r = 10 \times 5\sqrt{2} = 50\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$.

question_text: A light ray is incident at an angle of $60^\circ$ on one face of a prism of refractive angle $90^\circ$. If the light ray grazes the second face, then the refractive index of the material of the prism is
solution: At the grazing face, $r_2 = C$ where $\sin C = \frac{1}{\mu}$. Since $r_1 = 90^\circ - C$, Snell's law at first face gives $\sin 60^\circ = \mu \cos C = \sqrt{\mu^2 - 1}$. Thus, $\frac{3}{4} = \mu^2 - 1 \implies \mu = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$.

question_text: A boy with defective eyesight cannot see things beyond $50\text{ cm}$. The corrective lens required has the power
solution: For myopia, to see an object at infinity, $f = -d = -50\text{ cm} = -0.5\text{ m}$. Hence, the power is $P = \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{-0.5\text{ m}} = -2\text{ D}$.

Two thin convex lenses of focal lengths $20\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$ are placed $10\text{ cm}$ apart. The power of the combination of lenses is
solution: Powers are $P_1 = \frac{100}{20} = 5\text{ D}$ and $P_2 = \frac{100}{5} = 20\text{ D}$. The net power is $P = P_1 + P_2 - d P_1 P_2 = 5 + 20 - (0.10)(5)(20) = 15\text{ D}$.
